subject: GPU runway — deal alignment & activation phases

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: GPU runway — proposed activation phases for HLX-2387

Hi Alice / Helix ops team,

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, I attached a short playbook with three reservation options (Conservative, Growth, Aggressive) and a sample ramp schedule we think matches Helix’s phased rollout. High level: 

- Conservative: 16 GPUs min (2x 8-GPU pods), canary for first 30 days, gradual 3-month ramp to 64 GPUs for peak inference.
- Growth: 32 GPUs min (4x 8-GPU pods), 6-week canary, scale to 128 GPUs over 8–12 weeks with scheduled burst windows.
- Aggressive: 64 GPUs min (8x 8-GPU pods), 2-week canary, faster ramp (4–6 weeks) to 256 GPUs for production ML ops.

We also included recommendations on warm-start credits (to offset cold-cache warmup), suggested autoscale guardrails, and a fallback model variant for low-cost routing if capacity spikes.

Please review the attached "redwood_reserve_playbook_v1.pdf" and the Helix workbook I started (helix_capacity_workbook.xlsx). Happy to walk through the workbook on a follow-up call — we can map the phases to your product launch dates and traffic forecast.

Next steps I propose:
1) Helix to confirm target go-live window and peak concurrency estimate.
2) Redwood to finalize a canary plan and SLA addendum for the chosen option.
3) Schedule a checklist review with Helix infra/ops for network/KMS items.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

3) Credits: how are warm-start credits applied, and is there a way to reconcile them monthly?

Also attaching a rough traffic projection for our first two quarters (see helix_capacity_workbook.xlsx). We’re leaning toward Growth but want clarity on the soft-start path if actual traffic undershoots.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: GPU runway — proposed activation phases for HLX-2387

Hi Alice + team —

Answers inline and added a few operational constraints: 

1) Minimums / Soft-start: We can support a soft-start of 8 GPUs behind a contract that includes a 16-GPU SLA floor that becomes effective at T+60 days. Practically that means: customer pays for the 16-GPU minimum from day 1 at a discounted holdback rate (we typically apply a 30% reduction to the difference during the soft-start period). If Helix confirms lower consumption after 60 days, we can re-negotiate commitments for months 3–6 (but the SLA floor will have applied).

2) Canary acceptance criteria: 
- Latency P95 <= 250ms for inference payloads at target payload mix
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx + model failures) over a rolling 24h window
- No data-plane security incidents during canary window
If canary fails, automatic rollback to a pre-agreed fallback model + extended canary of 7 days while we remediate.

3) Warm-start credits: Credits are applied as token-hour offsets on the monthly invoice (one accounting line). We can show Helix a monthly reconciliation report that maps daily warm-start usage to credits consumed. Credits expire after the contract month. If you prefer multi-month reconciliation we can put that into the agreement as a billing term.

Operational notes: automatic prefix/KV caching will shortcut most warmups but for cold-starts we recommend a 48–72 hour pre-warm window for large-scale batch migrations. Burst windows can be scheduled (up to 6 hours/day, 48 hours/month included in Growth plan). Additional burst beyond included limits is billed at the on-demand uplift rate.

Attached a short "activation checklist" we use to validate infra readiness and a sample capacity timetable (included in helix_capacity_workbook.xlsx).

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in quick internal approval guidance on discounts and SLA tweaks:

- We can approve the soft-start 8->16 GPU structure for deals up to $350k ARR with a 30% holdback discount as Karthik outlined.
- For Growth option (32->128 GPUs) we can offer a 10% committed discount on unit token cost and one-time warm-start credit equivalent to 48 GPU-hours to help with migration.
- SLA addendum: standard 99.9% uptime with a 30-day SLA carve-out window during canary (document draft attached as proposed_sla_addendum.docx). Any escalation beyond that requires VP sign-off.
